previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was readmitted one day after discharge due to fever, leukocytosis, and abdominal pain, concerning for a urinary tract infection. He has a chronic indwelling Foley catheter and a history of multidrug-resistant UTIs. Urine cultures grew pan-sensitive Proteus and multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, prompting a switch from ceftriaxone to ciprofloxacin. His mental status and symptoms improved with appropriate antibiotics. Constipation recurred, but resolved with continued aggressive bowel regimen after a bowel movement on hospital day 4. His blood cultures remained negative, and chest imaging showed atelectasis without pneumonia. Lisinopril was restarted for blood pressure control, and he was discharged to a rehab facility on a full course of ciprofloxacin and optimized home medications.

# Urinary Tract Infection: On presentation he was complaining of 
suprapubic pain and general malaise. His UA was concerning for 
UTI, and he was empirically started on ciprofloxacin. Urine 
culture showed Klebsiella, which was sensative to cipro. He was 
maintained on this antibiotic for a total course of 7 days. 
During this hospitalization we discussed his case with ID, who 
recommended outpatient follow-up to discuss the need for 
antibiotic suppressive therapy, given his chronic foley and 
multiple recent UTIs. Upon discharge his suprapubic pain had 
improved. 

# Depression/Anxiety: He appeared very depressed, apathetic, and 
withdrawn. He stated that he did not enjoy going to day care 
because he does not enjoy being around people. Additionally, he 
reported numerous somatic complaints during this 
hospitalization, and peserverated about death. Similar to his 
last admission, he did not tolerate being left alone for very 
long. He was maintained on his home regimen of antidepressants 
including citalopram and duloxetine. 

# CAD: He is s/p CABG, stenting, and porcine aortic valve 
replacement and is followed by Dr. ___ at ___. He had 
a brief episode of chest pain lasting for approximately 5 
minutes, with radiation to his jaw. During this episode he 
appeared to be very anxious. At this time EKG showed no changes, 
and cardiac enzymes were at his baseline. Repeat enzymes were 
again at his baseline. He was continued on his home metoprolol, 
ASA, and atorvastatin. 
  
# Constipation. The patient has a chronic problem with 
constipation, and his recent admission on ___ was primarily for 
constipation. He was continued on an aggressive bowel regiment 
of standing Senna, Colace, and Miralax with bisacodyl and milk 
of magnesia prn, and bisacodyl suppository.

# Hypertension: No active issues on this hospitalization. He was 
maintained on his home regimen of lisinopril and metoprolol.

# Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Diet controlled. No active issues on 
this hospitalization. 

# Penile Ulcer: Persistent on this admission; reduced in size 
based on prior descriptions. He denies any associated 
complaints, and there were no signs of infection. The ulcer was 
treated with bacitracin.

# Bladder spasm: His suprapubic pain was most likely secondary 
to his UTI, and improved with treatment. He was maintianed on 
his home dose of Tolterodine.

# GERD: No active issues on this hospitalization. He was 
continued on his home omeprazole.
